issues.legal_issue: A court exercising constitutional writ jurisdiction may decline to decide a disputed claim of earlier government possession when the evidence does not satisfactorily establish that possession.
material_facts: The appellant alleged that the Forest Department had taken possession of the lands in 1953 or 1954.

The documents relied on included statements by a forest officer that possession had been taken, but the officer explained that he had made them under an erroneous impression about the effect of forest notifications.

The High Court found the evidence insufficient to decide whether possession had been taken, and the Supreme Court agreed that it was justified in declining to decide the factual dispute in the writ proceedings.
issues.conclusion: The High Court was justified in declining to decide whether the Government had taken possession in 1953 or 1954; the appellant remained free to pursue any other remedy available under law.
issues.legal_principle: A disputed factual question that cannot be conclusively decided on the evidence before a court in proceedings under Article 226 need not be determined in those proceedings. The Court left open any other remedy available under law.

predicates.constitutional_writ_proceeding: The claimant seeks relief in a constitutional writ proceeding.
predicates.disputed_prior_possession: The claimant alleges that the government took possession before the acquisition proceedings, and that allegation is disputed.
predicates.insufficient_evidence: The evidence before the court does not satisfactorily establish whether the government took that possession.

issues.definition: When a claimant raises disputed earlier government possession in a constitutional writ proceeding and the evidence is insufficient, the court may decline to determine that factual issue.

issues.legal_issue: In an urgent land acquisition, a declaration of urgency or publication of a public notice alone does not vest land in the Government under the provision for taking possession before an award; the Government must direct the taking of possession and the Collector must take possession in accordance with that provision.
material_facts: The Government invoked the urgency procedure and dispensed with the proceedings for objections before issuing the acquisition declaration.
A public notice was issued, but the record did not establish that the Government directed the Collector to take possession or that the Collector took possession under the urgency procedure.
A note in the acquisition officer’s order sheet contemplated delivery of possession, but there was no evidence that the order was implemented.
The appellant argued that prior possession, the acquisition declaration, or expiry of the period after the public notice meant that the land had vested in the Government.
issues.conclusion: The lands did not vest in the Government merely because of the urgency declaration, the public notice, or expiry of the period following that notice; the record showed neither the required direction nor possession taken under the urgency procedure.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 16 and 17(1) of the Land Acquisition Act, land vests absolutely when the Collector takes possession under the applicable provision. Section 17(1) permits possession before an award only in a case of urgency, when the appropriate Government directs it, and after the prescribed period from publication of the section 9(1) notice. The words “whenever the appropriate Government so directs” concern the taking of possession, not merely the declaration of urgency. The Court explained and distinguished Lt. Governor of Himachal Pradesh v. Avinash Sharma: that case involved earlier possession together with the relevant action under section 17, whereas no such action was shown here.

rule.if: land_acquisition_proceeding and urgency_declared and public_notice_published and (not government_directed_possession or not collector_took_possession)

predicates.land_acquisition_proceeding: The case concerns land sought to be acquired by the Government.
predicates.urgency_declared: The Government declares urgency in connection with the acquisition.
predicates.public_notice_published: A public notice concerning the persons interested in the land is published.
predicates.government_directed_possession: The Government directs the Collector to take possession under the urgency procedure.
predicates.collector_took_possession: The Collector actually takes possession under the urgency procedure.

issues.definition: In an urgent acquisition proceeding, if a public notice has been published but the Government has not directed possession or the Collector has not taken it, the land does not vest under the urgency procedure.

issues.legal_issue: The Government may withdraw land from acquisition if possession has not been taken under the applicable vesting provisions.
material_facts: The Government withdrew a substantial portion of the lands that had been notified for acquisition after deciding that acquiring the entire area was not worthwhile.
The appellant sought compensation for the withdrawn lands.
The record did not establish possession taken under section 17(1), and the alleged earlier possession was not satisfactorily proved in the writ proceedings.
issues.conclusion: The Government was competent to withdraw the lands from acquisition because possession under the applicable vesting provisions had not been established; the appeals were dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 48(1) of the Land Acquisition Act permits the Government to withdraw from acquisition any land of which possession has not been taken, subject to the exception in section 36, which was not relevant. For this purpose, possession means possession taken under section 16 or section 17(1); until such possession is taken, the land does not vest absolutely in the Government. Lt. Governor of Himachal Pradesh v. Avinash Sharma was distinguished because the relevant possession and statutory action were present there but not established here.

rule.if: land_acquisition_proceeding and government_withdrew_from_acquisition and not possession_taken_under_vesting_procedure

predicates.land_acquisition_proceeding: The case concerns land sought to be acquired by the Government.
predicates.government_withdrew_from_acquisition: The Government withdraws the land from the acquisition.
predicates.possession_taken_under_vesting_procedure: The Collector has taken possession of the land under a procedure that vests it in the Government.

issues.definition: When the Government withdraws land from an acquisition proceeding before possession has been taken under a vesting procedure, it may withdraw the land from acquisition.
